pivotal_trials.design: 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (Study 201) followed by open-label extension (Study 202); 3 arms: eteplirsen 30 mg/kg/wk (n=4), eteplirsen 50 mg/kg/wk (n=4), placebo (n=4); placebo patients crossed over to eteplirsen at Week 24
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary (Study 201): change from baseline in percent dystrophin-positive fibers in muscle biopsy; Primary (Study 202): 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) at Week 48; post hoc comparison of 12 eteplirsen-treated patients vs. 13 external historical controls up to Week 144
pivotal_trials.result: No statistically significant difference between eteplirsen and placebo on 6MWT at Week 24 (pre-specified ITT analysis negative) or Week 48 (pre-specified ITT analysis negative); dystrophin by Western blot ~0.93% of normal at Week 180; post hoc comparison to external historical controls showed ~162-meter difference in 6MWT (p=0.0005) but deemed uninterpretable due to major methodological limitations; AdCom voted 7 No / 6 Yes on substantial evidence of dystrophin benefit and 7 No / 3 Yes on substantial clinical evidence of efficacy

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-site; direct intramuscular injection of eteplirsen (0.09 mg or 0.9 mg) or placebo into foot muscle in 7 DMD patients
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Exon 51 skipping in mRNA; dystrophin expression by Western blot and immunofluorescence
pivotal_trials.result: Clear dose-response: exon 51 skipping and dystrophin expression in all 5 patients at 0.9 mg (44–79% dystrophin-positive fibers by IF); no effect at 0.09 mg or placebo

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, IV once weekly for 12 weeks at doses up to 20 mg/kg in DMD patients
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent dystrophin-positive fibers in muscle biopsy
pivotal_trials.result: Mean dystrophin-positive fibers increased from ~2% at baseline to up to 19% at 20 mg/kg; no clear dose-response; high variability (2 mg/kg: +12% absolute increase; 4 mg/kg: decrease); study deemed inconclusive due to major methodological issues

advisory_committee.vote: 7-6 against substantial evidence of dystrophin benefit; 7-3 against substantial clinical evidence of efficacy (with 3 abstentions) — Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee, April 25, 2016

key_safety: In 114 total patients exposed, serious adverse events were few and generally disease-related (wound infection, ankle/femur fracture, post-operative vomiting); one patient had possibly drug-related cardiomyopathy (pre-existing); common AEs in controlled phase included upper respiratory infections (9 vs. 1 placebo), non-serious injuries (11 vs. 0 placebo), and prolonged aPTT in 2/4 patients in the 50 mg/kg arm; no renal toxicity signal observed clinically.
target_moa: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) that induces skipping of exon 51 in dystrophin pre-mRNA, restoring the reading frame and enabling production of a truncated but potentially functional dystrophin protein

_meta.indication: EXONDYS 51 is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle observed in some patients treated with EXONDYS 51. A clinical benefit of EXONDYS 51 has not been established. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification of a clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

indication_details.population_restrictions: confirmed mutation of the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping

advisory_committee_detail.vote: Not explicitly stated in the provided text
advisory_committee_detail.discussion_summary: The Advisory Committee met on April 25, 2016 to consider eteplirsen for DMD. The review text references the AC meeting primarily in the context of procedural concerns about the Center Director's 'extensive involvement in planning and participating' in the meeting, rather than detailing the AC's substantive scientific deliberations or vote outcome. The broader review documents deep disagreement among FDA reviewers about whether dystrophin as a surrogate endpoint was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, given serious flaws in biopsy quality, assay validation, and the absence of well-controlled randomized trials.

linkages.concern: Poor quality of many biopsies and failure of the sponsor to implement a high-quality procedure for assay validation led to a situation in which only a fraction of the data could be used to make the regulatory decision
linkages.change: Approval conditioned on accelerated approval pathway with required confirmatory post-marketing trial to verify clinical benefit

linkages.concern: Data from primate studies suggest a substantial increase in dose (approximately a log order) might produce the 10% of normal dystrophin levels considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit; human studies at higher doses have not been conducted

Risk of lowering the bar for new drug approval under accelerated approval pathway, with concern that approving on the basis of a surrogate endpoint with a trivial treatment effect could discourage development of effective therapies and encourage premature approvals for other serious conditions
linkages.change: Approval granted under accelerated approval with stipulations including a required confirmatory trial; Commissioner noted this unique situation would not set a general precedent

linkages.concern: Extensive, early involvement of the Center Director in the review process, including in planning and participating in the Advisory Committee meeting, appeared to upend the typical review and decision-making process
